THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE  COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:2044  CRL.P No. 13390 of 2023  ORDER

This petition is filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., praying to enlarge the petitioner/accused Nos.2 and 3 on bail in Crime No.553/2023 of Bellanduru Police Station registered for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 304B read with Section 34 of IPC.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and learned HCGP for the State.
Perused the material on record.

3. In the complaint lodged by one Kumaraswamy, father of deceased Shravani, it is alleged that marriage of his daughter was performed with accused No.1 - Mahesh on 15.10.2021 at V.R.Kalyana Mantap, BEML Nagar, KGF, by spending about Rs.18 Lakhs.
At the time of marriage, as per the demand made by the accused persons, gold ornaments weighing 150 grams were given as dowry.

After the marriage, his daughter was residing along with her husband and in-laws and for about 3 to 4 months, she was looked after properly, but thereafter she was subjected to physical NC:
2024:KHC:2044 and mental torture on the ground that no sufficient dowry was given and the gold ornaments given were not of good quality.
Further, the accused persons were demanding to provide a new bike and they were ill-treating her.
On 24.09.2023, they quarrelled with her in connection with dowry and drove her out of the house and therefore she was staying in the house of the complainant at Bengaluru.
Even thereafter, the accused used to make phone calls demanding dowry and ill-treating her.
On 09.11.2023, in view of the physical and mental torture meted to her by the accused persons, she committed suicide by hanging herself using a saree.
4. A perusal of the complaint averments would reveal that on 24.09.2023, the deceased came to her parents' house and she was residing with her parents at Bengaluru.
The incident took place on 09.11.2023 in the house of her parents.
It is alleged that on account of the physical and mental torture meted to the deceased, she committed suicide by hanging.
The petitioners are the parents-in-law of the deceased.
Omnibus allegations are made against them alleging they too were ill-treating the deceased.
Specific allegations are against accused No.1 that, even after the deceased came to her parental house, he was making phone calls and ill-treating her saying that she should bring cash and gold.
At this stage, there is no sufficient material to show that soon before her death, the deceased was subjected to cruelty by the petitioners i.e., accused Nos.2 and 3.
The petitioners are arrested and interrogated.

They are not required for further Shanthamma vs State Of Karnataka on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106618504/
